references.text: The blood of Cain's brother cries out from the ground, and the ground is cursed because of the blood that was shed on it. This illustrates how innocent blood defiles the land.
God demands human blood from the one who sheds it. Whoever sheds human blood, by humans shall their blood be shed. This establishes the principle of atonement through the murderer's blood.
The land becomes unclean because of sin and vomits out its inhabitants. This shows how sin, including bloodshed, defiles the land.
Innocent blood must not be shed in the land, for it will bring guilt of blood upon the people. The murderer must die to cleanse the land.
A ritual cleansing is required when a slain person is found and the murderer is unknown. This shows the need for atonement when blood has been shed on the land.
Innocent blood was shed and defiled the land. The psalmist describes how guilt of blood pollutes the earth.
The earth shall reveal the blood that has been shed upon it and no longer hide the slain. This confirms that guilt of blood remains on the land until it is atoned for.
Without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness. This New Testament principle reflects the Old Testament teaching that blood is necessary for atonement.
